sources.title: Incidents managed for Guàrdia Urbana  in the city of Barcelona
Incidents managed for Guàrdia Urbana  in the city of Barcelona

method: IRIS incidents and complaints (not queries/suggestions) with coordinates, last 24 months available, mapped to categories by AREA/ELEMENT/DETALL rules.
Residents per H3 cell: padró population per census section spread evenly over the section's area (20 m sample lattice).
Per-cell rate = (count + ½·neighbour counts + 1000·city rate) / (residents + ½·neighbour residents + 1000): ring smoothing plus shrinkage toward the city rate.

Crime: Mossos 'fets penals coneguts' (street-relevant types) per district (ABP), last 24 months; split over barris by 50% Guàrdia Urbana public-order incidents share + 50% population share; rate per resident shrunk toward the city rate (2000 residents).
Values are city-wide percentiles (0 = cleanest/safest, 100 = worst) against cells with ≥100 residents. Score = 100 − weighted mean of percentiles.
caveats: Complaints measure reporting, not reality: dense, central and tourist areas report more, and some neighbourhoods rarely use IRIS.
Normalising by residents inflates areas with few residents and many visitors (old town, commercial streets).
Crime is official only at district level (10 Mossos ABPs); the within-district split is an estimate from city-police incident counts.
Data is not live: see the date ranges. IRIS and police data lag by several months.
Cells with fewer than 100 residents (parks, port, industrial land) are flagged low-population; their values are mostly the city average.
